title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 40, 'Paraphrase in terms of (topologico-isotopic) fundamental groups of Legendre's theory'. Grothendieck tests the idea on discrete groups first. Legendre's theory relates elliptic curves (type (1,1)) to genus-0 data via the λ-line.

Step 1, the (1,1) side. C^{ext}_{1,1} is the groupoid of discrete groups 'of type (1,1) with loop structure'. Its typical object is Π_{1,1} = ⟨x,y,l | [x,y]l = 1⟩. This is the free group F_2, with the peripheral class l = [x,y]^{-1}. The groupoid is connected, so it is equivalent to the groupoid of torsors under the automorphism group of one object. Here that group is Autext_lin(Π_{1,1}), the outer automorphisms respecting the loop structure. The marginal insert presumably names it the Teichmüller-type group T_{1,1}.

Step 2, the identification (50)-(51). Send an outer automorphism to its action on the abelianization (Π_{1,1})_ab ≅ Z². By Nielsen, Out(F_2) → GL(2,Z) is an isomorphism. Every automorphism of F_2 sends [x,y] to a conjugate of [x,y]^{±1}, so the loop condition costs nothing. Hence Autext(Π_{1,1}) ≅ GL(2,Z).

Step 3, the (0,3) side (previous page). C_{0,3} is equivalent to torsors under Aut_ext(Π_{0,3}), asserted there to be ≅ T_{0,3} ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1 =: GP(1,Z), i.e. PGL(2,Z).

Step 4, the Legendre functor (52)-(53). Grothendieck defines L: C^{ext}_{1,1} → C_{0,3} as the unique functor, up to canonical isomorphism, making the square commute with Tors(GL(2,Z)) → Tors(GP(1,Z)). The bottom arrow is change of structure group along the canonical projection GL(2,Z) → GL(2,Z)/±1 (54).

Step 5, the next page. Since this projection has kernel the center {±1}, L is not an equivalence. Dividing the groupoid by the universal central automorphism −id (the elliptic involution) gives C^{ext'}_{1,1} ≃ C_{0,3}. This is the groupoid-theoretic shadow of the classical facts:
- the elliptic involution acts trivially on moduli;
- M_{1,1} is the quotient of the λ-line (genus 0, level 2) by S_3;
- π_1^{orb}(M_{1,1}) = SL(2,Z) maps to PSL(2,Z), and with orientation reversal GL(2,Z) maps to PGL(2,Z).

The whole construction is formal: connected groupoid ≃ Tors(automorphism group), and a group homomorphism induces a functor. The content is in the identifications of the automorphism groups.
errors: (54) as transcribed/written reads GP(1,Z) ≃ GL(1,Z)/±1. It must be GL(2,Z)/±1 = PGL(2,Z), as the next page confirms (Gl(2,Z)' = Gl(2,Z)/(±1) ≃ Gp(1,Z)). This is a slip.

Gap/ambiguity: if C_{0,3} means free groups of rank 2 with the full structure of three peripheral conjugacy classes (up to permutation and inversion), its outer automorphism group is finite, about S_3 × Z/2 (≅ GL(2,F_2) × Z/2). It would not be PGL(2,Z), and as a bare free group its Out is GL(2,Z). So the identification Aut_ext(Π_{0,3}) ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1 (asserted on the previous page) needs a specific, unstated reading of 'lacets fléchés' (e.g. tangential/orbifold data, or really the λ-line/(0,4) situation). As written on this page it is not justified.
L is not an equivalence; Grothendieck recognises this on the next page by quotienting by the central −id. No error on this page itself, just an intermediate step.

ideas.what: Out of the once-punctured-torus group Π_{1,1} ≅ F_2 is identified with GL(2,Z) via the action on the abelianization Z²; every outer automorphism preserves the boundary loop class up to inversion
ideas.modern_name: Dehn–Nielsen–Baer for the once-punctured torus; Nielsen's theorem Out(F_2) ≅ GL(2,Z)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the treatment of the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 1 in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (unsure of exact location)

ideas.what: A connected groupoid of 'groups with loop structure' of a given type is equivalent to torsors under its outer automorphism group; functors between such groupoids are induced by changing the structure group
ideas.modern_name: Connected groupoid ≃ BG; change of structure group (pushforward of torsors)
ideas.where_published: Standard torsor formalism in SGA 1/SGA 4 and Giraud; used throughout La Longue Marche

ideas.what: A 'Legendre functor' from discrete groups of type (1,1) to groups of type (0,3), inducing GL(2,Z) → PGL(2,Z), which becomes an equivalence after killing the central elliptic involution −id
ideas.modern_name: Group-theoretic form of the Legendre/λ-line relation: M_{1,1} vs. genus-0 moduli with level-2 structure; SL(2,Z) → PSL(2,Z) and rigidification by the generic ±1 automorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); orbifold/stack version standard (e.g. rigidification of M_{1,1}, Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} vs M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower in low dimension; whether this exact 'Legendre functor' formalism appears elsewhere: unsure

missed.claim: This is an explicitly groupoid/torsor-theoretic 'paraphrase of Legendre's theory'. It sets up a canonical functor between the type-(1,1) and type-(0,3) loop-group groupoids, with an equivalence after rigidifying by −id. It is presented as a warm-up for a profinite/Galois-equivariant version that would compare the Galois actions on π_1 of M_{1,1} and of genus-0 moduli. The mathematics on this page is classical. The documentary interest is that Grothendieck frames the genus 1 ↔ genus 0 comparison as a functor between groupoids of 'groups with loops' (his 'équation des lacets' programme).
missed.quote: On a donc un foncteur canonique L : C^{ext}_{1,1} → C_{0,3} ... de "Legendre"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it documents how Grothendieck intended to transport genus-1 information into genus 0 within the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme. This parallels later work comparing GT-actions in genus 0 and genus 1 (Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez's elliptic associators), but adds no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (Out(F_2) ≅ GL(2,Z), torsor description of connected groupoids, GL(2,Z) → PGL(2,Z) and rigidification by the elliptic involution) is classical. The only interest is the framing as a 'Legendre functor' between loop-group groupoids within the équation-des-lacets programme. The page also contains an imprecise identification of Aut_ext(Π_{0,3}).
transcription_corrections: (54): the right-hand side should read GP(1,Z) ≃ GL(2,Z)/±1 (Grothendieck's hand looks like 'GL(1,Z)/±1', but GL(2,Z) is meant; cf. next page).
The inserted '𝒞_{1,1} ≃' above the first line is likely '𝔗_{1,1} ≃' (the Teichmüller-type group, parallel to 𝔗_{0,3} on the previous page), naming the group before 'Autext_lin(π_{1,1})'.
(52): the 'A' before C^{ext}_{1,1} appears to be a struck or false start; read L : C^{ext}_{1,1} → C_{0,3}.
Marginal note near (52) reads approximately 'L, initiale de "Legendre"' (L as the initial of Legendre).
Previous page 'C_{1,1}^{cat}' should be 'C_{1,1}^{ext}', consistent with this page.
Subscript 'lin' in Autext_lin is uncertain; it might be 'l.' (for 'lacets'), i.e. outer automorphisms respecting the loop structure.
